Moderate-intensity exercise: 50–70% max heart rate (max HR ≈ 220 − age); can talk but not sing; slight sweating. Examples: brisk walking (5–6 km/h), leisure cycling, slow swimming, yoga, housework.
High-intensity exercise: 70–85%+ max heart rate; can only say short phrases; heavy sweating, muscle fatigue. Examples: running (8+ km/h), HIIT, fast cycling, competitive sports, fast stair climbing.

Quick self-test for exercise intensity: talk test (full sentences vs. few words), sing test (can vs. cannot), sweat level, recovery time. Example for age 30: max HR ≈ 190, moderate zone 95–133 bpm, high intensity ≥133 bpm.
The mall_project Django app is located at D:\AgentLongTaskTest\6.9\mall_project\ and uses app_name='products' namespace for the products app URLs.
When a Django app uses app_name (app namespace), URL names in reverse/redirect calls must use the 'app_name:url_name' format (e.g., 'products:product_list'), not just the bare URL name.
The mall_project root URL (path '') redirects to 'products:product_list' to serve as the homepage.

Login brute-force protection: track failed attempts per username in session, lock account for 30 minutes after 5 consecutive failures, show red error message below password field with remaining attempts count, clear failures on successful login.
Registration page user type radio buttons aligned using flexbox (inline-flex) for vertical centering with label text, replacing default block layout that caused misalignment.

Key files modified: accounts/views.py (login_view with lockout logic), templates/accounts/login.html (red error display), templates/accounts/register.html (radio button alignment fix). All 25 tests passed.

For Django session-based brute-force protection, store attempt counts and lockout timestamps in request.session keyed by username. Check lockout before authenticating, increment on failure, reset on success.

Django's default RadioSelect widget renders options vertically as <ul><li> list. To render horizontally, create a custom widget subclassing RadioSelect with a custom template that uses inline-flex labels instead of list items.

Custom HorizontalRadioSelect widget defined in accounts/forms.py using template 'accounts/horizontal_radio.html'. Template iterates widget.subwidgets rendering each as an inline label with radio input.

Used custom widget template approach (subclassing RadioSelect with template_name override) rather than inline CSS hacks to fix vertical radio button layout, as the root cause was the <ul><li> HTML structure.

Django RadioSelect widget uses template 'django/forms/widgets/radio.html' and wraps content in <fieldset><legend> tags when use_fieldset=True (default). Custom render() method returning raw HTML may still be wrapped by the parent _render() template system.

When styling Django forms with CSS, `.form-group input { width: 100% }` affects radio buttons and causes visual distortion. Must scope selectors to text/email/password inputs only, and add `input[type="radio"] { width: auto; }` to preserve radio button sizing.
Custom widget `HorizontalRadioSelect` is defined in mall_project/accounts/forms.py, overriding RadioSelect.render() to output inline labels with radio inputs.
CSS styles for the project are in mall_project/templates/base.html. Key selectors: `.form-group input`, `.form-group > label`, `.form-group fieldset`, `.form-group fieldset label`.

The cart app uses app_name='cart' in its urls.py, so all URL reverse lookups must use 'cart:cart', 'cart:add_to_cart', etc.

In Django, when an app defines app_name in urls.py, all {% url %} template tags and reverse() calls must include the namespace prefix (e.g., 'cart:cart' not just 'cart'), otherwise NoReverseMatch is raised.
products/views.py had two redirect('product_list') calls that needed to be redirect('products:product_list') due to app namespace.

Django e-commerce mall project located at D:\AgentLongTaskTest\6.9\mall_project\. Uses SQLite, has apps: accounts, products, orders, cart. Run with `python manage.py runserver`, init data with `python manage.py init_data`.
Seller order list must query via OrderItem.objects.filter(product__seller=request.user) to get order IDs, then filter Order by those IDs. Order.user only refers to the buyer, not the seller.

init_data command must call set_password() and set is_superuser=True/is_staff=True unconditionally after get_or_create, not only when created=True, to ensure password is always correct even if user already exists.

In Django, Order.objects.filter(user=request.user) only returns orders where request.user is the buyer. To find orders where the user is the seller, must go through the OrderItem -> product -> seller relationship.
Django management command get_or_create only applies defaults when created=True. To guarantee password/flags are always set, perform updates and save() unconditionally after the get_or_create call.
Admin credentials: username=admin, password=admin123. Must run `python manage.py init_data` after server restart to reset admin password.

The mall project (D:\AgentLongTaskTest\6.9\mall_project) uses a custom User model with `user_type` field (CUSTOMER, etc.) and Django's `is_superuser` flag. The admin user is created with `user_type=User.UserType.CUSTOMER` in `init_data`, so filtering only by `user_type` is insufficient to isolate real customers.
When querying customer lists in Django, always exclude superusers with `is_superuser=False` even when filtering by `user_type`, because admin accounts may share the same `user_type` value.
Customer list query location: `accounts/views.py` around line 146. Correct pattern: `User.objects.filter(user_type=User.UserType.CUSTOMER, is_superuser=False).select_related("wallet")`
